cases.description: Choose the customer's own callback number among three regex-found numbers.

request.state: Ticket #4471 from Dana Whitfield: 'My router keeps dropping. Please call me back on 415-555-0142. Our office line is 415-555-0199 but nobody answers it after 5. Your support line 1-800-555-0100 was busy.'

callback.instructions: Which candidate is the number the customer asks to be called back on?

criteria.415-555-0142: the customer's own number where they want the callback
criteria.not_stated: the ticket gives no callback number

cases.description: Only the vendor's number appears; the customer's own number is not stated, so the not_stated option must win.

request.state: Ticket #4472 from Sam: 'Refund never arrived. Ring your billing team on 1-800-555-0100 if you need anything from me, otherwise just email me.'

callback.instructions: Which candidate is a phone number belonging to the customer?

criteria.1-800-555-0100: a number that belongs to the customer
criteria.not_stated: no number belonging to the customer appears in the text

cases.description: Multi-question request: verify three extracted fields at once (two correct, one hallucinated).

request.state: Order confirmation. Order ID: A-88213. Customer: Priya Nair. Shipping to 12 Elm Street, Leeds. Items: 2x USB-C cable. Estimated delivery: 3-5 business days.

order_id.instructions: Extracted order_id = 'A-88213'. Does the text contain this exact string as the order ID?

criteria.true: the text states this order ID
criteria.false: the text does not state this order ID

city.instructions: Extracted city = 'Leeds'. Does the text contain this exact string as the shipping city?

criteria.false: the text does not state this city

carrier.instructions: Extracted carrier = 'DHL'. Does the text name DHL as the carrier?

criteria.true: the text names DHL as the carrier
criteria.false: the text does not name DHL

cases.description: Dates read as text: pick the weekday component from a phrase; arithmetic then stays in code.

request.state: Hi, can we meet Friday after next? Anything in the afternoon works.

weekday.instructions: Which weekday does the sender name?

offset.instructions: Which week offset does the phrase express? 'this' = the coming one, 'next' = one week later, 'after_next' = two weeks later.

criteria.next: the occurrence in the following week

daypart.instructions: Which part of the day is requested?

cases.description: No date in the text; the year component must resolve to not_stated rather than guessing.

request.state: Contract signed on the 3rd of March by both parties. Payment is due within thirty days.

year.instructions: Which year is the contract signing date in?

criteria.not_stated: the year is not stated in the text

cases.description: NER by classification: code proposes spans, model classifies each span type (batched questions).

request.state: Yesterday Marie Curie Hospital in Lyon announced that Dr. Alain Perrot will lead the new oncology unit.

span_a.instructions: In the sentence, what kind of entity is the span 'Marie Curie Hospital'?

span_b.instructions: In the sentence, what kind of entity is the span 'Lyon'?

span_c.instructions: In the sentence, what kind of entity is the span 'Alain Perrot'?

cases.description: Span boundary selection: choose the candidate that is exactly brand plus model, excluding the generic category words that follow.

request.state: Review: I bought the Logitech MX Master 3S wireless mouse last month and the scroll wheel is fantastic.

product.instructions: A product name is the brand and model only. Generic category nouns such as 'wireless mouse' are never part of a product name. Which candidate span is the product name in the review?

criteria.Logitech MX Master 3S: brand and complete model, ending at '3S' and stopping before any category noun
criteria.MX Master: cuts the name short: missing the brand and the '3S'
criteria.Logitech MX Master 3S wireless mouse: wrong: runs past the model into the generic category words 'wireless mouse'

cases.description: Counting pattern done right: code finds each 'error' match with its context, the model classifies each match (real failure vs harmless mention); code counts the answers.

[3] error: disk full on /var
[4] retry policy: error budget is 2%

criteria.true: the line reports an actual failure
criteria.false: the line only mentions the word error

m2.instructions: Match [2] '0 errors found in lint run'. Is this line reporting a real failure that happened?

criteria.true: the line reports an actual failure
criteria.false: the line only mentions the word error

m3.instructions: Match [3] 'error: disk full on /var'. Is this line reporting a real failure that happened?

criteria.true: the line reports an actual failure

criteria.true: the line reports an actual failure
